prompt.text: A SOC analyst notices that several endpoints have logs with timestamps that drift by several minutes from the SIEM. Before correlating events across hosts, which configuration MUST be corrected first?
prompt.html: A SOC analyst notices that several endpoints have logs with timestamps that drift by several minutes from the SIEM. Before correlating events across hosts, which configuration MUST be corrected first?

options.label: B
options.text: Synchronize all sources to a common NTP time source
options.html: Synchronize all sources to a common NTP time source

options.label: C
options.text: Enable full-packet capture on each endpoint
options.html: Enable full-packet capture on each endpoint

options.label: D
options.text: Switch all logs to JSON format
options.html: Switch all logs to JSON format

explanation: Synchronize all sources to a common NTP time source ensures every event shares a consistent clock so the SIEM can accurately order and correlate activity across hosts. Why the other options are wrong: Increase log retention to 365 days : longer retention preserves history but does nothing to align mismatched timestamps for correlation. Enable full-packet capture on each endpoint : packet capture adds data volume yet cannot fix clock drift between sources. Switch all logs to JSON format : a uniform format aids parsing but timestamps remain skewed without time synchronization.
explanationHtml:
Synchronize all sources to a common NTP time source ensures every event shares a consistent clock so the SIEM can accurately order and correlate activity across hosts.
Why the other options are wrong:Increase log retention to 365 days: longer retention preserves history but does nothing to align mismatched timestamps for correlation.Enable full-packet capture on each endpoint: packet capture adds data volume yet cannot fix clock drift between sources.Switch all logs to JSON format: a uniform format aids parsing but timestamps remain skewed without time synchronization.

prompt.text: An analyst must verify that archived security logs have not been altered since collection. Which property is the analyst validating?
prompt.html: An analyst must verify that archived security logs have not been altered since collection. Which property is the analyst validating?

explanation: Log integrity confirms that stored records remain unchanged from the time of collection, typically verified with hashing or write-once storage. Why the other options are wrong: Log retention : retention governs how long logs are kept, not whether their contents were tampered with. Log verbosity : verbosity controls the level of detail captured, which is unrelated to proving the data is unmodified. Log rotation : rotation cycles log files by size or age and does not establish that records are authentic.
explanationHtml:
Log integrity confirms that stored records remain unchanged from the time of collection, typically verified with hashing or write-once storage.
Why the other options are wrong:Log retention: retention governs how long logs are kept, not whether their contents were tampered with.Log verbosity: verbosity controls the level of detail captured, which is unrelated to proving the data is unmodified.Log rotation: rotation cycles log files by size or age and does not establish that records are authentic.

prompt.text: A SOC is overwhelmed by raw logs from hundreds of devices and wants a single platform to aggregate, normalize, and correlate them for alerting. Which tool BEST meets this need?
prompt.html: A SOC is overwhelmed by raw logs from hundreds of devices and wants a single platform to aggregate, normalize, and correlate them for alerting. Which tool BEST meets this need?

options.label: A
options.text: A standalone syslog file on each host
options.html: A standalone syslog file on each host

explanation: A SIEM platform centrally ingests, normalizes, and correlates log data from many sources to generate prioritized security alerts. Why the other options are wrong: A standalone syslog file on each host : per-host files keep data siloed and offer no cross-source correlation or alerting. A vulnerability scanner : a scanner finds weaknesses on assets but does not aggregate and correlate operational logs. A password vault : a vault secures credentials and has no role in log aggregation or analysis.
explanationHtml:
A SIEM platform centrally ingests, normalizes, and correlates log data from many sources to generate prioritized security alerts.
Why the other options are wrong:A standalone syslog file on each host: per-host files keep data siloed and offer no cross-source correlation or alerting.A vulnerability scanner: a scanner finds weaknesses on assets but does not aggregate and correlate operational logs.A password vault: a vault secures credentials and has no role in log aggregation or analysis.

prompt.text: An analyst hardening a Linux server wants to ensure only required services run at boot. Which action MOST directly reduces the attack surface?
prompt.html: An analyst hardening a Linux server wants to ensure only required services run at boot. Which action MOST directly reduces the attack surface?

options.label: B
options.text: Disable and remove unnecessary services and daemons
options.html: Disable and remove unnecessary services and daemons

options.label: D
options.text: Add the server to a load balancer
options.html: Add the server to a load balancer

explanation: Disable and remove unnecessary services and daemons shrinks the attack surface by eliminating listening services an attacker could exploit. Disable and remove unnecessary services and daemons shrinks the attack surface by eliminating listening services an attacker could exploit.
Why the other options are wrong:Increase the swap file size: swap affects memory management and has no bearing on exposed services.Enable verbose kernel logging: more logging improves visibility but does not remove the services that create exposure.Add the server to a load balancer: load balancing distributes traffic and does not reduce the host's running services.

prompt.text: While reviewing a Windows host, an analyst sees that the file system uses FAT32 on a partition holding sensitive data. Why is this a hardening concern?
prompt.html: While reviewing a Windows host, an analyst sees that the file system uses FAT32 on a partition holding sensitive data. Why is this a hardening concern?

options.label: A
options.text: FAT32 lacks native access control lists and encryption support
options.html: FAT32 lacks native access control lists and encryption support

options.label: C
options.text: FAT32 cannot store files larger than 1 KB
options.html: FAT32 cannot store files larger than 1 KB

options.label: D
options.text: FAT32 prevents any logging from occurring
options.html: FAT32 prevents any logging from occurring

explanation: FAT32 lacks native access control lists and encryption support , so sensitive data cannot enforce per-user permissions or use EFS the way NTFS allows. Why the other options are wrong: FAT32 cannot store files larger than 1 KB : FAT32 supports files up to 4 GB, so this size claim is false. FAT32 automatically encrypts every file : FAT32 has no encryption capability at all, the opposite of this claim. FAT32 prevents any logging from occurring : the file system does not block OS or application logging.
explanationHtml:
FAT32 lacks native access control lists and encryption support, so sensitive data cannot enforce per-user permissions or use EFS the way NTFS allows.
Why the other options are wrong:FAT32 cannot store files larger than 1 KB: FAT32 supports files up to 4 GB, so this size claim is false.FAT32 automatically encrypts every file: FAT32 has no encryption capability at all, the opposite of this claim.FAT32 prevents any logging from occurring: the file system does not block OS or application logging.

Delivery is the stage where the attacker transmits the weaponized payload to the victim, such as emailing a malicious attachment.
Why the other options are wrong:Weaponization: weaponization is coupling an exploit with a payload to build the malicious file, which happens before it is sent.Exploitation: exploitation occurs only after delivery when the victim opens the attachment and the code executes.Reconnaissance: reconnaissance is the earlier research used to identify the target, not the act of transmitting the payload.

options.label: C
options.text: A designated risk owner or management with authority to accept risk
options.html: A designated risk owner or management with authority to accept risk

Any passerby in the hallway : an uninvolved person cannot make a binding risk decision. explanationHtml:
A designated risk owner or management with authority to accept risk must approve, because risk acceptance is a management decision with accountability.
Why the other options are wrong:The on-call help desk technician: help desk staff lack the authority to formally accept organizational risk.Any passerby in the hallway: an uninvolved person cannot make a binding risk decision.The external scanner vendor: the vendor supplies tooling and has no authority over the customer's risk acceptance.

options.label: A

options.html: Wait for the regular change board with no interim measures

options.label: B
options.text: Disable the entire production environment indefinitely

options.label: C

options.html: Mark the finding informational and close it

options.label: D
options.text: Recommend an emergency change with a temporary compensating control to reduce exposure now
options.html: Recommend an emergency change with a temporary compensating control to reduce exposure now

Disable the entire production environment indefinitely : a total shutdown causes disproportionate business harm beyond the single finding. Mark the finding informational and close it : downgrading a confirmed critical RCE misrepresents real risk.
explanationHtml:
Recommend an emergency change with a temporary compensating control to reduce exposure now balances urgent internet-facing risk against the functionality impact while pursuing a permanent fix.
Why the other options are wrong:Wait for the regular change board with no interim measures: leaving a critical internet-facing RCE exposed for two weeks is indefensible.Disable the entire production environment indefinitely: a total shutdown causes disproportionate business harm beyond the single finding.Mark the finding informational and close it: downgrading a confirmed critical RCE misrepresents real risk.

prompt.html: An executive asks why the 'critical findings' count rose this quarter even though the team patched more than ever. Which explanation is MOST likely and should be included in the report narrative?

options.label: A

options.html: Newly disclosed CVEs and expanded scan coverage introduced more findings than were closed

explanationHtml:
Newly disclosed CVEs and expanded scan coverage introduced more findings than were closed explains how counts can rise despite strong remediation effort.
Why the other options are wrong:The scanner was unplugged: a disabled scanner would lower, not raise, the count of findings.All employees changed passwords: password changes do not generate new vulnerability findings.The report font was changed: formatting has no effect on the number of findings discovered.

prompt.html: A finding sits on a legacy system that cannot be patched, is contractually maintained by a third party, and supports a critical 24/7 process. The analyst must report the obstacle accurately. Which combination of inhibitors is present?

options.label: B
options.text: Legacy system, contractual constraint, and business process interruption
options.html: Legacy system, contractual constraint, and business process interruption

explanation: Legacy system, contractual constraint, and business process interruption accurately captures all three overlapping obstacles described. Why the other options are wrong: False positive and excessive metrics : the finding is valid and the issue is not metric volume, so these do not apply. Bandwidth and latency only : network performance is not what blocks remediation here. No inhibitors apply : clearly several real inhibitors are present, so this is incorrect.
explanationHtml:
Legacy system, contractual constraint, and business process interruption accurately captures all three overlapping obstacles described.
Why the other options are wrong:False positive and excessive metrics: the finding is valid and the issue is not metric volume, so these do not apply.Bandwidth and latency only: network performance is not what blocks remediation here.No inhibitors apply: clearly several real inhibitors are present, so this is incorrect.

prompt.text: Two stakeholders demand contradictory remediation timelines: the app owner wants 90 days for stability, while the CISO mandates 14 days for a critical internet-facing flaw. How should the analyst proceed in the report?
prompt.html: Two stakeholders demand contradictory remediation timelines: the app owner wants 90 days for stability, while the CISO mandates 14 days for a critical internet-facing flaw. How should the analyst proceed in the report?

options.label: C
options.text: Escalate the conflict with both positions and a risk-based recommendation to the deciding authority
options.html: Escalate the conflict with both positions and a risk-based recommendation to the deciding authority

options.label: D
options.text: Average the two timelines without context
options.html: Average the two timelines without context

explanation: Escalate the conflict with both positions and a risk-based recommendation to the deciding authority surfaces the disagreement for an accountable decision rather than the analyst arbitrarily choosing. Why the other options are wrong: Pick the longer timeline silently : silently favoring stability over a critical flaw hides risk from decision-makers. Refuse to document either timeline : omitting the conflict leaves stakeholders without the information to decide. Average the two timelines without context : a blind average ignores the severity-driven urgency and provides no justification.
explanationHtml:
Escalate the conflict with both positions and a risk-based recommendation to the deciding authority surfaces the disagreement for an accountable decision rather than the analyst arbitrarily choosing.
Why the other options are wrong:Pick the longer timeline silently: silently favoring stability over a critical flaw hides risk from decision-makers.Refuse to document either timeline: omitting the conflict leaves stakeholders without the information to decide.Average the two timelines without context: a blind average ignores the severity-driven urgency and provides no justification.

prompt.text: An organization's SLA says criticals are remediated in 7 days, but the metric counts a finding 'closed' when a ticket is opened, not when the fix is verified. What is the BEST correction to make the KPI meaningful?
prompt.html: An organization's SLA says criticals are remediated in 7 days, but the metric counts a finding 'closed' when a ticket is opened, not when the fix is verified. What is the BEST correction to make the KPI meaningful?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep counting closure at ticket creation
options.html: Keep counting closure at ticket creation

options.label: C
options.text: Count closure when the report is printed
options.html: Count closure when the report is printed

options.label: D
options.text: Measure closure only when remediation is validated and the vulnerability no longer appears
options.html: Measure closure only when remediation is validated and the vulnerability no longer appears

explanation: Measure closure only when remediation is validated and the vulnerability no longer appears ensures the KPI reflects actual risk reduction, not just administrative activity. Why the other options are wrong: Keep counting closure at ticket creation : opening a ticket does not reduce risk, so the metric would overstate success. Stop tracking SLAs entirely : abandoning SLA tracking removes accountability rather than improving accuracy. Count closure when the report is printed : printing is unrelated to whether the vulnerability is actually fixed.
explanationHtml:
Measure closure only when remediation is validated and the vulnerability no longer appears ensures the KPI reflects actual risk reduction, not just administrative activity.
Why the other options are wrong:Keep counting closure at ticket creation: opening a ticket does not reduce risk, so the metric would overstate success.Stop tracking SLAs entirely: abandoning SLA tracking removes accountability rather than improving accuracy.Count closure when the report is printed: printing is unrelated to whether the vulnerability is actually fixed.

prompt.html: A risk scorecard rolls all findings into one color: 'green.' An auditor notes a critical finding has been open 120 days yet the unit still shows green. What scorecard design flaw does this reveal?

options.label: A
options.text: Aggregation logic that lets aging critical findings be masked by many low-severity passes
options.html: Aggregation logic that lets aging critical findings be masked by many low-severity passes

options.label: B
options.text: The color uses the wrong shade of green
options.html: The color uses the wrong shade of green

options.label: C
options.text: Too many fonts in the legend
options.html: Too many fonts in the legend

explanation: Aggregation logic that lets aging critical findings be masked by many low-severity passes is the flaw, because a true critical exposure should never roll up to green. Why the other options are wrong: The color uses the wrong shade of green : the problem is the weighting logic, not the exact hue displayed. Too many fonts in the legend : typography does not cause a critical finding to be hidden. The scorecard is printed double-sided : printing format is irrelevant to the masking of risk.
explanationHtml:
Aggregation logic that lets aging critical findings be masked by many low-severity passes is the flaw, because a true critical exposure should never roll up to green.
Why the other options are wrong:The color uses the wrong shade of green: the problem is the weighting logic, not the exact hue displayed.Too many fonts in the legend: typography does not cause a critical finding to be hidden.The scorecard is printed double-sided: printing format is irrelevant to the masking of risk.

prompt.html: An analyst must brief both the board and the engineering team on the same critical campaign of findings. What is the BEST reporting strategy?

options.label: A

options.html: Send one identical highly technical document to both

options.label: B
options.text: Produce a layered report: an executive summary for the board and a technical appendix for engineers
options.html: Produce a layered report: an executive summary for the board and a technical appendix for engineers

options.label: C

options.html: Tell engineers verbally and skip the board

options.label: D

options.html: Only report to whichever group responds first

Tell engineers verbally and skip the board : omitting the board denies leadership needed risk visibility. Only report to whichever group responds first : selective reporting leaves a required stakeholder uninformed.
explanationHtml:
Produce a layered report: an executive summary for the board and a technical appendix for engineers tailors detail to each audience while keeping a single source of truth.
Why the other options are wrong:Send one identical highly technical document to both: dense technical content fails to communicate risk to the board.Tell engineers verbally and skip the board: omitting the board denies leadership needed risk visibility.Only report to whichever group responds first: selective reporting leaves a required stakeholder uninformed.

prompt.text: Leadership wants a single KPI that signals whether the organization is accumulating unaddressed risk over time. Which KPI BEST meets this need?
prompt.html: Leadership wants a single KPI that signals whether the organization is accumulating unaddressed risk over time. Which KPI BEST meets this need?

options.label: C
options.text: Average age of open critical and high findings (backlog aging)
options.html: Average age of open critical and high findings (backlog aging)

explanation: Average age of open critical and high findings (backlog aging) directly shows whether serious risk is piling up unaddressed over time. Number of dashboards created : dashboard count is an output metric unrelated to backlog risk. Count of report recipients : distribution size says nothing about lingering vulnerabilities.
explanationHtml:
Average age of open critical and high findings (backlog aging) directly shows whether serious risk is piling up unaddressed over time.
Why the other options are wrong:Total scans run this year: scan volume measures activity, not the accumulation of unresolved risk.Number of dashboards created: dashboard count is an output metric unrelated to backlog risk.Count of report recipients: distribution size says nothing about lingering vulnerabilities.

prompt.text: A patch is available and applies cleanly, but the system owner refuses to schedule downtime during the only available window because it overlaps end-of-month billing. The analyst's report should classify the primary inhibitor as which, and recommend what?
prompt.html: A patch is available and applies cleanly, but the system owner refuses to schedule downtime during the only available window because it overlaps end-of-month billing. The analyst's report should classify the primary inhibitor as which, and recommend what?

options.label: A
options.text: Patch availability; wait for a vendor fix
options.html: Patch availability; wait for a vendor fix

options.label: D
options.text: Business process interruption; negotiate an alternate window or interim mitigation
options.html: Business process interruption; negotiate an alternate window or interim mitigation

Legacy system; decommission immediately : nothing indicates the system is end-of-life, and abrupt decommissioning is unwarranted. False positive; close the finding : the finding is valid, so closing it as a false positive is wrong.
explanationHtml:
Business process interruption; negotiate an alternate window or interim mitigation correctly names the operational-disruption inhibitor and offers a practical path forward.
Why the other options are wrong:Patch availability; wait for a vendor fix: a working patch already exists, so availability is not the inhibitor.Legacy system; decommission immediately: nothing indicates the system is end-of-life, and abrupt decommissioning is unwarranted.False positive; close the finding: the finding is valid, so closing it as a false positive is wrong.

prompt.html: An analyst is pressured by a business unit to omit an unresolved critical finding from the quarterly report to avoid an audit flag. What is the MOST ethical and professional response?

options.html: Include the finding accurately and document the unit's position separately if needed

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.html: Replace it with a fabricated low-severity item

options.label: D

options.html: Delete the finding from the scanner database

Include the finding accurately and document the unit's position separately if needed preserves report integrity while still capturing stakeholder context.
Why the other options are wrong:Omit the finding to keep the peace: leaving out a known critical risk falsifies the report and exposes the organization.Replace it with a fabricated low-severity item: fabricating data is dishonest and a serious integrity violation.Delete the finding from the scanner database: destroying the record conceals real risk and undermines the audit trail.

prompt.text: After remediating a finding, what is the MOST reliable way to confirm the vulnerability is actually resolved?
prompt.html: After remediating a finding, what is the MOST reliable way to confirm the vulnerability is actually resolved?

options.label: A
options.text: Assume the patch worked once installed
options.html: Assume the patch worked once installed

options.label: B
options.text: Perform a validation rescan and confirm the finding no longer appears
options.html: Perform a validation rescan and confirm the finding no longer appears

options.label: D
options.text: Ask the user if it feels faster
options.html: Ask the user if it feels faster

explanation: Perform a validation rescan and confirm the finding no longer appears objectively verifies that remediation succeeded. Why the other options are wrong: Assume the patch worked once installed : installation does not guarantee the vulnerability is gone, as configuration may still expose it. Close the ticket without testing : closing without verification can leave an unresolved risk recorded as fixed. Ask the user if it feels faster : perceived speed has no relationship to whether the vulnerability is remediated.
explanationHtml:
Perform a validation rescan and confirm the finding no longer appears objectively verifies that remediation succeeded.
Why the other options are wrong:Assume the patch worked once installed: installation does not guarantee the vulnerability is gone, as configuration may still expose it.Close the ticket without testing: closing without verification can leave an unresolved risk recorded as fixed.Ask the user if it feels faster: perceived speed has no relationship to whether the vulnerability is remediated.

prompt.text: Which remediation approach involves applying an alternative control because the primary fix cannot be implemented, and should be documented as such in reporting?
prompt.html: Which remediation approach involves applying an alternative control because the primary fix cannot be implemented, and should be documented as such in reporting?

explanation: Compensating control is the alternative measure applied when the primary fix is infeasible and must be recorded with its residual risk. Why the other options are wrong: Full patch deployment : a full patch is the primary fix itself, not an alternative used when patching is impossible. Permanent decommission : decommissioning removes the asset entirely rather than mitigating it in place. Ignoring the finding : ignoring a finding is not a control and leaves the risk unaddressed.
explanationHtml:
Compensating control is the alternative measure applied when the primary fix is infeasible and must be recorded with its residual risk.
Why the other options are wrong:Full patch deployment: a full patch is the primary fix itself, not an alternative used when patching is impossible.Permanent decommission: decommissioning removes the asset entirely rather than mitigating it in place.Ignoring the finding: ignoring a finding is not a control and leaves the risk unaddressed.

prompt.text: A patch was applied and the dashboard shows the finding 'remediated,' but a manual test still triggers the vulnerability. What is the analyst's BEST next action before updating reports?
prompt.html: A patch was applied and the dashboard shows the finding 'remediated,' but a manual test still triggers the vulnerability. What is the analyst's BEST next action before updating reports?

options.label: A
options.text: Trust the dashboard and report it fixed
options.html: Trust the dashboard and report it fixed

options.label: C
options.text: Lower the severity to match the dashboard
options.html: Lower the severity to match the dashboard

options.label: D
options.text: Reopen the finding, investigate why the patch is ineffective, and report accurate status
options.html: Reopen the finding, investigate why the patch is ineffective, and report accurate status

explanation: Reopen the finding, investigate why the patch is ineffective, and report accurate status ensures reporting reflects the true, still-exploitable condition. Why the other options are wrong: Trust the dashboard and report it fixed : the manual test proves it is not fixed, so reporting it resolved is inaccurate. Hide the manual test results : concealing evidence of an unresolved flaw misrepresents real risk. Lower the severity to match the dashboard : adjusting severity to fit the tool ignores the demonstrated exploitability.
explanationHtml:
Reopen the finding, investigate why the patch is ineffective, and report accurate status ensures reporting reflects the true, still-exploitable condition.
Why the other options are wrong:Trust the dashboard and report it fixed: the manual test proves it is not fixed, so reporting it resolved is inaccurate.Hide the manual test results: concealing evidence of an unresolved flaw misrepresents real risk.Lower the severity to match the dashboard: adjusting severity to fit the tool ignores the demonstrated exploitability.

prompt.text: An organization decides not to fix a low-severity finding on a system scheduled for retirement next month, and records the decision. Which risk response does this represent?
prompt.html: An organization decides not to fix a low-severity finding on a system scheduled for retirement next month, and records the decision. Which risk response does this represent?

explanation: Risk acceptance is choosing to knowingly tolerate a documented risk, appropriate here given the imminent retirement and low severity. Why the other options are wrong: Risk transference : transference shifts the risk to a third party, such as insurance, which is not what occurred. Risk avoidance : avoidance eliminates the activity causing the risk, but the system remains in use until retirement. Risk mitigation : mitigation reduces the risk through controls, whereas here no fix is being applied.
explanationHtml:
Risk acceptance is choosing to knowingly tolerate a documented risk, appropriate here given the imminent retirement and low severity.
Why the other options are wrong:Risk transference: transference shifts the risk to a third party, such as insurance, which is not what occurred.Risk avoidance: avoidance eliminates the activity causing the risk, but the system remains in use until retirement.Risk mitigation: mitigation reduces the risk through controls, whereas here no fix is being applied.

prompt.text: After a remediation cycle, the analyst must report effectiveness to leadership. Which combination BEST demonstrates that remediation efforts are actually reducing risk?
prompt.html: After a remediation cycle, the analyst must report effectiveness to leadership. Which combination BEST demonstrates that remediation efforts are actually reducing risk?

options.label: B
options.text: Validated closure rate plus declining backlog aging for critical findings
options.html: Validated closure rate plus declining backlog aging for critical findings

options.label: C
options.text: Total emails sent to the team
options.html: Total emails sent to the team

Total emails sent to the team : email volume reflects communication activity, not remediation effectiveness. Count of scans scheduled : scheduling scans is an input metric and does not show risk going down.
explanationHtml:
Validated closure rate plus declining backlog aging for critical findings together show both that fixes are verified and that serious risk is shrinking over time.
Why the other options are wrong:Number of tickets opened only: opening tickets measures intake, not verified risk reduction.Total emails sent to the team: email volume reflects communication activity, not remediation effectiveness.Count of scans scheduled: scheduling scans is an input metric and does not show risk going down.

prompt.text: An analyst confirms that a single endpoint has malware but has not yet determined scope. Following the incident response plan, what is the FIRST formal action the analyst should take to trigger the response process?
prompt.html: An analyst confirms that a single endpoint has malware but has not yet determined scope. Following the incident response plan, what is the FIRST formal action the analyst should take to trigger the response process?

options.label: A
options.text: Declare an incident and notify the incident response lead
options.html: Declare an incident and notify the incident response lead

options.label: C
options.text: Issue a press release to customers
options.html: Issue a press release to customers

options.label: D
options.text: Calculate the mean time to remediate
options.html: Calculate the mean time to remediate

Issue a press release to customers : external communication occurs only after scope and obligations are understood and is coordinated through PR and legal, not at first detection. Calculate the mean time to remediate : that metric is computed after remediation completes and plays no role in initiating the response.
explanationHtml:
Declare an incident and notify the incident response lead formally activates the response process so the right people and procedures engage immediately.
Why the other options are wrong:Draft the after-action report: the after-action report is a post-incident artifact written after containment and recovery, not the first triggering step.Issue a press release to customers: external communication occurs only after scope and obligations are understood and is coordinated through PR and legal, not at first detection.Calculate the mean time to remediate: that metric is computed after remediation completes and plays no role in initiating the response.

prompt.text: A breach exposed customer records, and the legal team confirms a regulatory reporting obligation applies. Which stakeholder must the analyst's reporting prioritize to meet a statutory notification deadline?
prompt.html: A breach exposed customer records, and the legal team confirms a regulatory reporting obligation applies. Which stakeholder must the analyst's reporting prioritize to meet a statutory notification deadline?

explanationHtml:
The applicable regulatory reporting agency must be notified within the statutory window to satisfy the legal obligation the legal team identified.
Why the other options are wrong:The marketing department: marketing supports messaging but has no statutory deadline to satisfy and is not a regulatory recipient.The vendor's sales representative: a vendor salesperson has no role in regulatory breach notification.The internal training team: the training team may later incorporate lessons learned but is not a recipient for mandatory breach reporting.

prompt.html: During a long-running investigation, the day-shift analyst is leaving and a night-shift analyst is taking over. Which item is MOST important to include in the shift handover?

options.label: C
options.text: A copy of the employee handbook
options.html: A copy of the employee handbook

options.label: D
options.text: Current incident status, open tasks, and pending actions

explanationHtml:
Current incident status, open tasks, and pending actions ensures the incoming analyst can continue work without losing context or duplicating effort.
Why the other options are wrong:The analyst's personal performance review: a performance review is an HR matter unrelated to operational continuity of the incident.The organization's annual security budget: budget figures do not help the next analyst pick up an active investigation.A copy of the employee handbook: the handbook contains no incident-specific state needed to continue the work.

explanationHtml:
Lessons learned reviews the response process to capture improvements, focusing on what worked and what should change.
Why the other options are wrong:Root cause analysis: RCA identifies the underlying technical cause of the incident, not a broad review of process effectiveness.Incident declaration: declaration is the opening step that activates response, not a closing review.Forensic imaging: imaging preserves evidence during investigation and is not a process-improvement meeting.

prompt.text: Two months after a phishing-driven breach, leadership asks why the attacker succeeded despite an email filter. The analyst determines a misconfigured filter rule allowed the spoofed domain through. Identifying that misconfiguration is the result of which activity?

prompt.text: A SOC manager wants a KPI showing what proportion of generated alerts turn out to be genuine threats: TP / (TP + FP). Which metric BEST provides this?

Not all typosquatting is directly malicious—some just redirect users to another site. URL shorteners make URLs shorter, often using easily typed replacement URLs, but they can also be used to conceal malicious links. HTTP redirects simply send traffic from one URL to another. DNS manipulation would rely on DNS rather than a typo.

DNS manipulation would rely on DNS rather than a typo.

prompt.text: NIST defines five major types of threat information in NIST SP 800-150, “Guide to Cyber Threat Information Sharing.” Indicators, which are technical artifacts or observables that suggest an attack is imminent, currently underway, or compromise may have already occurred. prompt.html:

  1. Indicators, which are technical artifacts or observables that suggest an attack is imminent, currently underway, or compromise may have already occurred.
  2. Tactics, techniques, and procedures that describe the behavior of an actor.
  3. Security alerts like advisories and bulletins.
  4. Threat intelligence reports that describe actors, systems, and information being targeted and the methods being used.

explanation: The more effort Frank puts into staying up-to-date with information by collecting threat information (5), monitoring for indicators (1), and staying up-to-date on security alerts (3), the stronger his organization’s security will be. prompt.text: Geoff wants to perform passive reconnaissance as part of an evaluation of his organization’s security controls. Which of the following techniques is a valid technique to perform as part of a passive DNS assessment?

options.label: A
options.text: A DNS forward or reverse lookup
options.html: A DNS forward or reverse lookup

explanation: Passive reconnaissance gathers information from public or third-party sources without directly interacting with the target’s systems in a way that generates traffic to them, and WHOIS fits this model because it retrieves domain registration and related administrative details from registrar and registry databases rather than querying the target’s DNS infrastructure. A DNS forward or reverse lookup is typically treated as active in security assessments because it initiates DNS queries that may reach the target’s authoritative name servers (or at least trigger outbound resolution activity) and can be logged. A zone transfer is clearly active because it directly requests an entire DNS zone from the target’s authoritative server and is both detectable and commonly blocked. Using Maltego is a tool choice rather than a specific passive DNS technique and, depending on the transforms used, may generate active queries, so it is not the best unambiguous answer for a passive DNS assessment.
explanationHtml: C. Passive reconnaissance gathers information from public or third-party sources without directly interacting with the target’s systems in a way that generates traffic to them, and WHOIS fits this model because it retrieves domain registration and related administrative details from registrar and registry databases rather than querying the target’s DNS infrastructure. A DNS forward or reverse lookup is typically treated as active in security assessments because it initiates DNS queries that may reach the target’s authoritative name servers (or at least trigger outbound resolution activity) and can be logged. A zone transfer is clearly active because it directly requests an entire DNS zone from the target’s authoritative server and is both detectable and commonly blocked. Using Maltego is a tool choice rather than a specific passive DNS technique and, depending on the transforms used, may generate active queries, so it is not the best unambiguous answer for a passive DNS assessment.

The statement that it is impossible to scan multiple systems with a single SSH command is wrong because SSH can be used to run a single remote command that itself targets many hosts, such as an nmap scan over an entire subnet.

Questions 132–134 refer to the following scenario:

Pete recently conducted a broad vulnerability scan of all the servers and workstations in his environment. He scanned the following three networks:

  • Screened subnet (DMZ) network that contains servers with public exposure
  • Workstation network that contains workstations that are allowed outbound access only
  • Internal server network that contains servers exposed only to internal systems

He detected the following vulnerabilities:

  • Vulnerability 1: A SQL injection vulnerability on a screened subnet (DMZ) server that would grant access to a database server on the internal network (severity 5/5)
  • Vulnerability 2: A buffer overflow vulnerability on a domain controller on the internal server network (severity 3/5)
  • Vulnerability 3: A missing security patch on several hundred Windows workstations on the workstation network (severity 2/5)
  • Vulnerability 4: A denial-of-service vulnerability on a screened subnet (DMZ) server that would allow an attacker to disrupt a public-facing website (severity 2/5)
  • Vulnerability 5: A denial-of-service vulnerability on an internal server that would allow an attacker to disrupt an internal website (severity 4/5)

Note that the severity ratings assigned to these vulnerabilities are directly from the vulnerability scanner and were not assigned by Pete.

explanation: Vulnerability scans can only provide a snapshot in time of a system’s security status from the perspective of the vulnerability scanner. explanationHtml: D. Vulnerability scans can only provide a snapshot in time of a system’s security status from the perspective of the vulnerability scanner. Deprioritizing the issue based solely on CVSS ignores the critical context of active exploitation and exploit likelihood, which are strong risk escalators. Implementing only compensating controls and waiting for a later maintenance cycle leaves an exposed, high-risk, externally reachable system vulnerable longer than necessary, even when a patch already exists. explanation: You might find this question a little confusing because the scenario seems to describe a directory traversal attack and that is not one of the answer choices. The key to successfully answering this question is understanding that a directory traversal attack is a type of local file inclusion (LFI) attack. LFI attacks allow a remote user to access files stored on a server. Directory traversal achieves the attacker’s goal of LFI by navigating the directory structure with navigation commands such as.. and / in the URL. Remote file inclusion (RFI) attacks use a similar approach but allow the attacker to execute code that is hosted on their own computer using the targeted server.
explanationHtml: C. You might find this question a little confusing because the scenario seems to describe a directory traversal attack and that is not one of the answer choices. Copying the virtual disk files while the machine is actively running produces an inconsistent image, because the files shift underneath you mid-copy as data is written. Escalating to management to suspend the system ignores the scenario’s core constraint, since business needs rule out suspending the machine, and a live snapshot makes suspension unnecessary anyway. And the Volatility Framework analyzes memory images rather than acquiring them, so it cannot capture a live machine completely; it pulls nothing from disk and would still need a separate acquisition step to produce the memory image it works on.

prompt.text: An organization running a containerized application in a public cloud environment discovers that one of its Kubernetes pods was compromised and used to mine cryptocurrency. By the time the security team begins its investigation, the pod has been automatically terminated and replaced by the orchestrator’s self-healing mechanism. What is the primary forensic challenge in this scenario?
prompt.html: An organization running a containerized application in a public cloud environment discovers that one of its Kubernetes pods was compromised and used to mine cryptocurrency. By the time the security team begins its investigation, the pod has been automatically terminated and replaced by the orchestrator’s self-healing mechanism. What is the primary forensic challenge in this scenario?

options.label: A
options.text: The replacement pod contains evidence from the compromised pod.
options.html: The replacement pod contains evidence from the compromised pod.

options.label: B
options.text: Cloud providers do not allow forensic imaging of container infrastructure.
options.html: Cloud providers do not allow forensic imaging of container infrastructure.

options.label: C
options.text: The ephemeral nature of the container means volatile evidence was lost when the pod was terminated.
options.html: The ephemeral nature of the container means volatile evidence was lost when the pod was terminated.

options.label: D
options.text: Kubernetes clusters cannot generate logs for individual pods.
options.html: Kubernetes clusters cannot generate logs for individual pods.

explanation: The primary challenge is that containers are ephemeral by design. Therefore, when the compromised pod was terminated and replaced, its filesystem, running processes, network connections, and in-memory artifacts were destroyed. Unlike traditional servers, containers do not persist state after termination unless explicitly configured to do so, making volatile evidence recovery impossible after the fact. The replacement pod is a fresh instance and does not inherit any data from the compromised pod. Cloud providers do allow various forms of forensic investigation, including disk snapshots and log retrieval, though the available evidence differs from traditional environments. Kubernetes can and does generate logs for individual pods through its logging architecture, and those logs may still exist in a centralized logging system even after the pod is gone.
explanationHtml: C. The primary challenge is that containers are ephemeral by design. Therefore, when the compromised pod was terminated and replaced, its filesystem, running processes, network connections, and in-memory artifacts were destroyed. Unlike traditional servers, containers do not persist state after termination unless explicitly configured to do so, making volatile evidence recovery impossible after the fact. The replacement pod is a fresh instance and does not inherit any data from the compromised pod. Cloud providers do allow various forms of forensic investigation, including disk snapshots and log retrieval, though the available evidence differs from traditional environments. Kubernetes can and does generate logs for individual pods through its logging architecture, and those logs may still exist in a centralized logging system even after the pod is gone.

prompt.text: Scott needs to verify that the forensic image he has created is an exact duplicate of the original drive. Which of the following methods is considered the current forensic standard?
prompt.html: Scott needs to verify that the forensic image he has created is an exact duplicate of the original drive. Which of the following methods is considered the current forensic standard?

explanation: Using a SHA-256 hash is considered the current forensic standard because it provides a much stronger, collision-resistant hashing method than older algorithms and is widely recommended in modern forensic practice for demonstrating image integrity. MD5 was historically popular, but known collision vulnerabilities reduce confidence in its use as a primary integrity check in contemporary cases, particularly where evidence may be legally challenged. SHA-1 is stronger than MD5 but has also been shown to be vulnerable to practical collision attacks, so it is similarly discouraged as a sole verification mechanism. Grouping all three together suggests they are equally acceptable as current standards, but present best practice emphasizes stronger algorithms such as SHA-256 for evidentiary reliability.
explanationHtml: C. prompt.text: Which of the following properly lists the order of volatility from least to most volatile?
prompt.html: Which of the following properly lists the order of volatility from least to most volatile?

options.label: A
options.text: Printouts, swap files, CPU cache, RAM
options.html: Printouts, swap files, CPU cache, RAM

options.label: B
options.text: Hard drives, USB media, DVDs, CD-RWs
options.html: Hard drives, USB media, DVDs, CD-RWs

options.label: C
options.text: DVDs, hard drives, virtual memory, caches
options.html: DVDs, hard drives, virtual memory, caches

explanation: DVDs, hard drives, virtual memory, caches is the proper order from least to most volatile because optical media like DVDs are long term, offline storage, hard drives are persistent but can be overwritten during normal operation, virtual memory (swap) is more transient as it is frequently changed to support active processes, and CPU caches are extremely short lived, disappearing as soon as power is lost or the processor state changes. The sequence with printouts, swap files, CPU cache, and RAM is wrong because printed documents are indeed very nonvolatile, but swap files are less volatile than RAM and CPU cache should be considered more volatile than RAM, not less. The list of hard drives, USB media, DVDs, and CD-RWs only compares relatively nonvolatile storage types and does not move meaningfully from least to most volatile. The sequence with RAM, swap files, SSDs, and printouts is inverted because RAM is far more volatile than swap, SSDs, or printed material, while printouts should be at the least volatile end rather than the most.
explanationHtml: C. DVDs, hard drives, virtual memory, caches is the proper order from least to most volatile because optical media like DVDs are long term, offline storage, hard drives are persistent but can be overwritten during normal operation, virtual memory (swap) is more transient as it is frequently changed to support active processes, and CPU caches are extremely short lived, disappearing as soon as power is lost or the processor state changes. The sequence with printouts, swap files, CPU cache, and RAM is wrong because printed documents are indeed very nonvolatile, but swap files are less volatile than RAM and CPU cache should be considered more volatile than RAM, not less. The list of hard drives, USB media, DVDs, and CD-RWs only compares relatively nonvolatile storage types and does not move meaningfully from least to most volatile. The sequence with RAM, swap files, SSDs, and printouts is inverted because RAM is far more volatile than swap, SSDs, or printed material, while printouts should be at the least volatile end rather than the most.

prompt.text: After a ransomware incident is fully contained and systems are restored, the IR lead holds a cross-team review meeting. The team documents what worked, identifies gaps in logging, updates the escalation matrix, and revises the ransomware playbook to include new decision points. prompt.html: After a ransomware incident is fully contained and systems are restored, the IR lead holds a cross-team review meeting. The team documents what worked, identifies gaps in logging, updates the escalation matrix, and revises the ransomware playbook to include new decision points. Which incident response phase best describes these activities?

explanation: These activities fall under post-incident because they occur after containment and recovery are complete and focus on documenting lessons learned, reviewing what succeeded or failed, and updating procedures, playbooks, and escalation paths to improve future responses. Preparation involves building capabilities before an incident occurs, such as creating initial playbooks and setting up tools, not revising them based on a specific event. Recovery is concerned with restoring systems and services to normal operation and validating that they are clean and functioning, which has already happened in this scenario. Analysis focuses on understanding the incident as it unfolds and shortly afterward to determine root cause, scope, and attacker behavior, while the described cross-team review is a structured, improvement-oriented follow-up characteristic of the post-incident phase.
explanationHtml: C. These activities fall under post-incident because they occur after containment and recovery are complete and focus on documenting lessons learned, reviewing what succeeded or failed, and updating procedures, playbooks, and escalation paths to improve future responses. Preparation involves building capabilities before an incident occurs, such as creating initial playbooks and setting up tools, not revising them based on a specific event. Recovery is concerned with restoring systems and services to normal operation and validating that they are clean and functioning, which has already happened in this scenario. Analysis focuses on understanding the incident as it unfolds and shortly afterward to determine root cause, scope, and attacker behavior, while the described cross-team review is a structured, improvement-oriented follow-up characteristic of the post-incident phase.

prompt.text: Jake is building a forensic image of a compromised drive using the dd command with its default settings. He finds that the imaging is going very slowly. What parameter should he adjust first?
prompt.html: Jake is building a forensic image of a compromised drive using the dd command with its default settings. He finds that the imaging is going very slowly. What parameter should he adjust first?

explanation: The most likely cause of this slowness is an incorrect block size. Block size is set using the bs flag and is defined in bytes. By default, dd uses a 512-byte block size, but this is far smaller than the block size of most modern disks. Using a larger block size will typically be much faster, and if you know the block size for the device you are copying, using its native block size can provide huge speed increases. This is set using a flag like bs=64k. The if and of flags adjust the input and output files, respectively, but there is no indication that these are erroneous. The count flag adjusts the number of blocks to copy and should not be changed if Jake wants to image the entire disk.
explanationHtml: B. The most likely cause of this slowness is an incorrect block size. Block size is set using the bs flag and is defined in bytes. By default, dd uses a 512-byte block size, but this is far smaller than the block size of most modern disks. Using a larger block size will typically be much faster, and if you know the block size for the device you are copying, using its native block size can provide huge speed increases. This is set using a flag like bs=64k. The if and of flags adjust the input and output files, respectively, but there is no indication that these are erroneous. The count flag adjusts the number of blocks to copy and should not be changed if Jake wants to image the entire disk.

explanation: Advanced persistent threats (APTs) are highly skilled attackers with advanced capabilities who are typically focused on specific objectives. To accomplish those objectives, they often obtain and maintain long-term access to systems and networks using powerful tools that allow them to avoid detection and to stay ahead of responders who attempt to remove them. A Trojan horse is simply malware disguised as something legitimate and does not by itself imply a prolonged, entrenched campaign. A rootkit is designed to hide malicious activity and can contribute to persistence, but it is a tool or technique rather than a broader attack pattern. A zero-day attack refers to the exploitation of an unknown vulnerability, which explains initial compromise but not the sustained, hard-to-remove intrusion over a period of years.
explanationHtml: B. Advanced persistent threats (APTs) are highly skilled attackers with advanced capabilities who are typically focused on specific objectives. To accomplish those objectives, they often obtain and maintain long-term access to systems and networks using powerful tools that allow them to avoid detection and to stay ahead of responders who attempt to remove them. A Trojan horse is simply malware disguised as something legitimate and does not by itself imply a prolonged, entrenched campaign. A rootkit is designed to hide malicious activity and can contribute to persistence, but it is a tool or technique rather than a broader attack pattern. A zero-day attack refers to the exploitation of an unknown vulnerability, which explains initial compromise but not the sustained, hard-to-remove intrusion over a period of years.

Therefore, a noncredentialed external scan would provide the least information.

A noncredentialed scan provides far less information than a credentialed scan or an agent-based scan because both credentialed and agent-based scans are able to gather configuration information from the target systems. External scans also provide less information than internal scans because they are filtered by border firewalls and other security devices. Therefore, a noncredentialed external scan would provide the least information.

prompt.text: After finishing a forensic case, Sam needs to wipe a magnetic hard drive (HDD) that he is using to prepare it for the next case. Which of the following methods is best suited to preparing the hard drive that he will use if he wants to be in compliance with NIST SP 800-88?
prompt.html: After finishing a forensic case, Sam needs to wipe a magnetic hard drive (HDD) that he is using to prepare it for the next case. Which of the following methods is best suited to preparing the hard drive that he will use if he wants to be in compliance with NIST SP 800-88?

options.label: C
options.text: Seven rounds: all ones, all zeros, and five rounds of random values.
options.html: Seven rounds: all ones, all zeros, and five rounds of random values.

explanation: NIST SP 800-88, along with many forensic manuals, requires a complete zero wipe of the drive but does not require multiple rounds of wiping. Degaussing is primarily used for magnetic media like tapes and renders a hard drive unusable, which would prevent Sam from using it for his next case. Reformatting the drive removes the file system references to data but leaves the data itself on the drive, where it may be recovered using forensic tools.
explanationHtml: B. NIST SP 800-88, along with many forensic manuals, requires a complete zero wipe of the drive but does not require multiple rounds of wiping. Degaussing is primarily used for magnetic media like tapes and renders a hard drive unusable, which would prevent Sam from using it for his next case. Reformatting the drive removes the file system references to data but leaves the data itself on the drive, where it may be recovered using forensic tools.

prompt.text: Adam finds entries in his authentication logs showing failed login attempts against many different user accounts across systems in his network. The attempts use the same small set of common passwords, such as “Password123,” “Winter2026,” and “CompanyName2026!” What type of attack has he discovered?
prompt.html: Adam finds entries in his authentication logs showing failed login attempts against many different user accounts across systems in his network. The attempts use the same small set of common passwords, such as “Password123,” “Winter2026,” and “CompanyName2026!” What type of attack has he discovered?

explanation:
Password spraying attacks try one or a small number of common passwords against many different accounts. This technique is often used to avoid account lockout mechanisms that would be triggered by many failed attempts against a single account. Credential stuffing attacks use stolen or compromised username and password combinations across multiple sites or services. Session hijacking requires the attacker to take over a valid authenticated session. An on-path attack requires the attacker to intercept traffic between two parties, allowing them to read or modify the traffic before it reaches its intended destination. 
Adam could mitigate password spraying attacks by using multifactor authentication, monitoring for widespread failed login attempts, rate limiting authentication attempts, blocking known malicious sources, and using backoff algorithms or account lockout policies carefully to reduce the likelihood of account lockout abuse.
explanationHtml:
D. Password spraying attacks try one or a small number of common passwords against many different accounts. This technique is often used to avoid account lockout mechanisms that would be triggered by many failed attempts against a single account. Credential stuffing attacks use stolen or compromised username and password combinations across multiple sites or services. Session hijacking requires the attacker to take over a valid authenticated session. An on-path attack requires the attacker to intercept traffic between two parties, allowing them to read or modify the traffic before it reaches its intended destination.

Adam could mitigate password spraying attacks by using multifactor authentication, monitoring for widespread failed login attempts, rate limiting authentication attempts, blocking known malicious sources, and using backoff algorithms or account lockout policies carefully to reduce the likelihood of account lockout abuse.

prompt.text: Rae wants to use digital signatures to verify that incoming messages genuinely originated from the domain they claim to be from, reducing the amount of spam that her organization receives. Which of the following techniques or methods will most directly fit her needs?
prompt.html: Rae wants to use digital signatures to verify that incoming messages genuinely originated from the domain they claim to be from, reducing the amount of spam that her organization receives. Which of the following techniques or methods will most directly fit her needs?

explanation: DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) uses digital signatures to validate that the claimed domain of the sender is the actual sender’s domain. Sender Policy Framework (SPF) records identify the mail servers that can send email from your domain but do not prove the sender’s domain. Spamhaus is an antispam organization, and an RBL is a real-time black hole list, which is a list of untrusted or spam-sending hosts.
explanationHtml: B. DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) uses digital signatures to validate that the claimed domain of the sender is the actual sender’s domain. Sender Policy Framework (SPF) records identify the mail servers that can send email from your domain but do not prove the sender’s domain. Spamhaus is an antispam organization, and an RBL is a real-time black hole list, which is a list of untrusted or spam-sending hosts.

prompt.text: Your organization recently suffered a series of serious vulnerabilities as a result of the use of legacy software that is no longer supported by the vendor. explanation: You should implement compensating controls that mitigate the risk of the legacy systems. Awareness, training, and education may be helpful, but it would not address the risk as completely as a compensating control. Patch management is not possible because the software is no longer supported by the vendor, so no new patches will be issued. Changing business requirements is not a feasible solution because the system is needed for 6 more months.
explanationHtml: B. You should implement compensating controls that mitigate the risk of the legacy systems. For example, you might place the systems on an isolated network where they are less susceptible to direct attack. Awareness, training, and education may be helpful, but it would not address the risk as completely as a compensating control. Patch management is not possible because the software is no longer supported by the vendor, so no new patches will be issued. Changing business requirements is not a feasible solution because the system is needed for 6 more months.

prompt.text: Gabby’s organization captures sensitive customer information, and salespeople and others often work with that data on local workstations and laptops. After a recent inadvertent breach where a salesperson accidentally sent a spreadsheet of customer information to another customer, her organization is seeking a technology solution that can help prevent similar problems. What should Gabby recommend?

explanation: Data loss prevention (DLP) can tag sensitive data and then scan outbound communications for that data. Once tagged data or data that matches specific patterns such as credit card numbers or Social Security numbers are discovered, DLP can alert the user or take other action. IDS, an intrusion detection system, might be able to detect patterns but could not stop traffic flow. FSB is not a security term, and full-disk encryption (FDE) can help prevent data loss if a system is stolen.
explanationHtml: C. Data loss prevention (DLP) can tag sensitive data and then scan outbound communications for that data. Once tagged data or data that matches specific patterns such as credit card numbers or Social Security numbers are discovered, DLP can alert the user or take other action. IDS, an intrusion detection system, might be able to detect patterns but could not stop traffic flow. FSB is not a security term, and full-disk encryption (FDE) can help prevent data loss if a system is stolen.

prompt.text: During a port scan of a server, Gwen discovered that the following ports are open on the internal network. TCP port 25

TCP port 80

TCP port 110

TCP port 443

TCP port 1521

TCP port 3389

explanation: Web servers commonly run on ports 80 (for HTTP) and 443 (for HTTPS). Database servers commonly run on ports 1433 (for Microsoft SQL Server), 1521 (for Oracle), or 3306 (for MySQL). Port 110 is the default TCP port used for the Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP3). Remote Desktop Protocol services commonly run on port 3389. Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) runs on port 25. There is no evidence that SSH, which uses port 22, is running on this server.
explanationHtml: C. Web servers commonly run on ports 80 (for HTTP) and 443 (for HTTPS). Database servers commonly run on ports 1433 (for Microsoft SQL Server), 1521 (for Oracle), or 3306 (for MySQL). Port 110 is the default TCP port used for the Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP3). Remote Desktop Protocol services commonly run on port 3389. Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) runs on port 25. There is no evidence that SSH, which uses port 22, is running on this server.

prompt.text: Jake wants to ensure that only authorized IP addresses can send email on behalf of his organization but doesn’t want to require certificates and signatures for the validation. What should he implement?
prompt.html: Jake wants to ensure that only authorized IP addresses can send email on behalf of his organization but doesn’t want to require certificates and signatures for the validation. What should he implement?

explanation: The Sender Policy Framework (SPF) allows you to create a list of authorized IP addresses that can send emails on an organization’s behalf. This is done by publishing and checking a SPF record maintained by the organization. Domain Keys Identified Mail (DKIM) uses public key cryptography and uses a private key to sign email headers. Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Compliance (DMARC) combines SPF and DKIM to validate senders and take actions based on a policy. Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) is a protocol for sending messages using digital signatures and encryption.
explanationHtml: D. The Sender Policy Framework (SPF) allows you to create a list of authorized IP addresses that can send emails on an organization’s behalf. This is done by publishing and checking a SPF record maintained by the organization. Domain Keys Identified Mail (DKIM) uses public key cryptography and uses a private key to sign email headers. Domain-Based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Compliance (DMARC) combines SPF and DKIM to validate senders and take actions based on a policy. Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) is a protocol for sending messages using digital signatures and encryption.
